name: What fill material is best for a pool fill-in?

mainEntity.name: What material should be used to fill in a swimming pool: clean fill dirt, gravel, sand, or decomposed granite?
mainEntity.text: What material should be used to fill in a swimming pool: clean fill dirt, gravel, sand, or decomposed granite?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no universal best fill material for every pool fill-in. Most projects need a compactable base material that can be placed in lifts and mechanically compacted to reduce future settling. Contractors may use fill dirt, crushed base, gravel, sand, or decomposed granite depending on drainage needs, soil conditions, and what will be built or planted above the filled area. The critical factor is not simply what goes in the hole, but whether the material is clean, structurally appropriate, and compacted properly. Poor-quality fill can settle unevenly, creating dips in lawn areas or problems under pavers and patios. In many cases, a layered approach works best, with drainage measures at the bottom and more stable graded material near the top. Homeowners should ask for the exact material specification, compaction method, and whether the contractor will certify the fill. If a future structure is planned, material choice should be coordinated with that design from the start.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best fill material depends on the site, drainage, and future use of the yard. Many contractors use compacted fill dirt with gravel or other drainage material, while some projects use sand or decomposed granite near the top layer. Clean, compactable material and proper layering matter more than one single product.
